newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish treasury ministry against tax on NFIs.
newsitem.headline: Polish treasury ministry against tax on NFIs.

text.p: Polish Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz said he would ask the Finance Minister not to scrap the tax exemption which the country's 15 National Investment Funds enjoy on gains from sales from their portfolios.
"I have come to a conclusion that introducing the tax would be a significant threat to the goals of the National Investment Funds programme," Pietrewicz told a conference of the funds on Wednesday.

The finance ministry plans to reintroduce in 1998 a 36 percent corporate tax on sales by the funds. It says that this is in line with the will of parliamentary committees which shaped the new income tax laws and rejected proposals to keep the NFI tax breaks.
Pietrewicz said the tax on NFI proceeds from selling their firms' stock would reduce their ability to invest in other firms from their portfolios.

News of the impending tax burden prompted a 10 percent fall of the mass privatisation programme's unit on the Warsaw bourse. The finance ministry's press office said it was still legally possible for the minister to re-introduce the tax break.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international consortia of managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.
